content: Every human being is a sculptor, chiseling his own character out of the marble of hardship.
author: Viktor Frankl
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

In Viktor Frankl's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
